name: NJM4580 / JRC4580 (incl. TI RC4580) (dual audio bipolar)
tagline: Japan's cheap 'standard audio op-amp' in countless sound cards, CD players and DACs; praised for a neutral, high-resolution 'plain as water' sound, rated above NE5532 by Soomal.
technology: Bipolar dual op-amp in the standard dual pinout (pin-compatible with 4558/5532-type duals), optimised for audio ('specially designed for improving tone control'): low noise, 15 MHz GBW, high output current, low THD, ±2 V minimum supply. NJM4580 input stage is PNP according to JP hobby notes and two NJR-labelled SPICE macromodels (medium confidence; datasheet equivalent circuit not read). TI RC4580 is a separate TI-made part whose input polarity is contested: Headphonesty says the RC4580-die NE5532 went from a PNP to an NPN input stage, while Rich Cabot and diyAudio posters describe the RC4580-die NE5532 as PNP-input. The classic NE5532 is commonly documented with an NPN input pair, so Headphonesty's direction may be reversed (inference, not checked this pass).
manufacturers: Nisshinbo Micro Devices (successor to New JRC, 2022-)
Texas Instruments (RC4580 second source, 2003-; RC4580-Q1 automotive)

lineage.role: second source (TI-made pin- and function-compatible part; die origin not documented)
lineage.notes: Datasheet SLOS412: first issued April 2003, then Rev C (March 2004), Rev D (November 2014) and Rev E (November 2024). RC4580-Q1 (SLOS707) followed in December 2010. TI RFAB PCNs 20240429005.1 (30 April 2024) and 20250129000.1 (3 February 2025) cover process/die revisions for select devices; PCN 20231114002.1 is reported as a bond-wire change. A TI E2E thread titled 'NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 all now the same die' (June 2026) and Rich Cabot ('they just relabeled a 4580', via Hackaday) indicate the RC4580 design is now the shared die.

reputation.summary: The default 'standard audio op-amp' in Japanese and Chinese consumer audio. Soomal found the JRC4580 in many mid- and high-end sound cards, active speakers, headphone amps and DACs, calling it 'not top-tier but better than the so-called king of op-amps NE5532' and describing it as high-resolution and neutral or plain ('平白如水'), adaptable but characterless, unlike the warm OP275. Japanese hobby sources call it the standard audio op-amp: fast and smooth with low residual noise, mellow and easy to listen to, though some find it overly smooth or veiled. Opinion is not uniform: nabe.adiary's CMoy comparison puts NJM4580 in C rank below NE5532 (B); a Chinese PC-audio primer calls it NE5532-like and average; English forums say it is chosen for price rather than performance, and some call it 'somewhat edgy and lacking detail'. Its ±2 V minimum supply makes it popular for USB-powered DIY; a 2012 srad.jp commenter ran the '50-yen NJM4580DD' straight from USB power.
sonic_descriptors: neutral / plain ('平白如水', '音色中性平淡' - Soomal)
high resolution ('解析力出色', '解析力高' - Soomal)
adaptable but characterless ('对声音的适应性强，但缺乏特点' - Soomal)
fast and smooth, low residual noise (JP hobby notes)
mellow and easy listening; to some, overly smooth or veiled (JP notes on NJM4580DD)
relatively flat with good HF extension (JP repair-shop note)
similar to NE5532, average (Chinese PC-audio primer, per search summary)
'somewhat edgy and lacking detail' (minority English-forum view)
typical_uses: Sound-card analog outputs (Soomal: TerraTec DMX 6Fire LT; TempoTec Hifier Fantasia / Variations / Sonata / X-Fi Rhapsody; Musiland Moli; 傲王 SQ717; AUDIOPROBE SPARTAN CUE 110)
Sound-card recording input gain stage (Musiland X-Sword II main card, per Soomal)
Headphone amps and DACs (Musiland HP10; TempoTec Fantasia DAII Plus unbalanced output)
Japanese CD players and AV gear (ONKYO / DENON / PIONEER per JP repair-shop notes)
DIY USB-powered DAC and headphone-amp stages (±2 V minimum supply)
Preamp, tone-control, active-filter and headphone-amp stages (datasheet target applications)
caveats: Not a high-end part. Soomal calls it good but not top-tier and characterless, nabe.adiary ranks it below NE5532, and a Chinese primer calls it average. The 'better than NE5532' verdict comes from one reviewer (Soomal).
Soomal says it is often confused with the far cheaper, pin-compatible JRC4558.
Nisshinbo gives no input noise current and only an RIAA-weighted noise figure (RS=2.2 kΩ, 30 kHz LPF); nV/√Hz is only a graph.
Nisshinbo's 20250303 datasheet marks NJM4580D (DIP8) and NJM4580L (SIP8) NRND. The D-rank DIP (NJM4580DD / D-D) is not addressed separately, and future DIP rolling stock may need SMD-to-DIP adapters.
TI RC4580 is a different part (GBW 12 vs 15 MHz). The reputation was earned by the JRC part; TI's NE5532, LM833 and MC33078 now reportedly use the RC4580 die.
The datasheet claims headphone-amp suitability (±13.5 V typ into 2 kΩ at ±15 V), but low-impedance headphones benefit from a buffer (general practice, not measured here).
The '50 yen' price comes from a 2012 comment; current prices were not checked.

silicon_changes.when: Process-migration PCN 20231114002.1 (15 Nov 2023) for NE5532DR/LM833DR/MC33078DR; production change 2024-2025 (SFAB to RFAB). NE5532 datasheet SLOS075K Dec 2025. TI E2E confirmation 2026; Hackaday 3 Jun 2026.
silicon_changes.identification: NE5532/NE5532A: SLOS075K (Dec 2025) documents the new silicon; SLOS075J (Jan 2015) and earlier describe the legacy die. RC4580 has no documented marker: its datasheet went to SLOS412E in Nov 2024 (change list not captured). No PCN was found saying that the RC4580 itself was re-fabricated or redesigned.
silicon_changes.summary: TI E2E thread 'NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 all now the same die' confirms the consolidation. Hackaday reports that Rich Cabot (Audio Precision co-founder) identified the RC4580 die in the new NE5532 ('they just relabeled a 4580'). Headphonesty reports field failures on boards with ±22 V-class rails, removal of the NE5532's input protection diodes, and halved HBM ESD. The E2E summary notes the classic NE5532 has back-to-back input diodes and the RC4580 does not. For RC4580 buyers this is the donor design, so little change is expected. The hazard is for TI NE5532, LM833 and MC33078 users, whose parts now behave like an RC4580-class device. JRC/Nisshinbo NJM4580 is not involved.

silicon_changes.audio_impact: No RC4580-specific audio change is documented. A post-2024 TI NE5532, LM833 or MC33078 behaves like an RC4580-class part (5 V/µs, ±18 V max, no input diodes), not like the classic 5532.

silicon_changes.summary: A TI E2E China thread ('RC4580: PCN change-Wire binding') and search summaries report that PCN 20231114002.1 changes the RC4580's bond wire from gold to copper. The same multi-device PCN covers the process migration of NE5532DR, SA5532ADR, LM833DR and MC33078DR, so for RC4580IDR the documented change is at assembly level, not a die change. A customer asked in that thread whether copper wire affects supply current; TI's answer was not captured.

The PCN's full device list was not seen directly. This corrects the earlier reading that PCN 20231114002.1 is only a bond-wire PCN: it also carries the NE5532/LM833/MC33078 process migration.

The Rev E change list was not captured. The datasheet feature bullet says 'Operating voltage ±2 V to ±18 V', while TI's product page uses 'Dual, 32-V' / '±2 V to ±16 V' wording; which of these changed, and when, is unconfirmed. PCN 20240429005.1 ('Qualification of RFAB using qualified Process Technology, Die Revision, Datasheet, and additional Assembly site/BOM options for select devices') and PCN 20250129000.1 (RFAB, HPA8 process, 300 mm, die change from process change) were found, but neither is confirmed to list RC4580.

silicon_changes.when: April 2003 (TI RC4580 introduced, SLOS412) to present
silicon_changes.identification: Tell them apart by part number and logo: TI RC4580 (orderables RC4580ID/IDR/IP/IPWR) versus JRC/NJR/Nisshinbo NJM4580, often called JRC4580 after its marking.
silicon_changes.summary: TI's RC4580 is a pin- and function-compatible second source. No evidence was found that it is a JRC die, and its GBW is lower. Its other headline figures match the NJM4580 (±2 to ±18 V, 0.8 µVrms, 5 V/µs, 0.0005% THD). Input polarity: the NJM4580 is PNP per NJR-labelled SPICE macromodels and Japanese notes. For TI's RC4580 it is disputed (Headphonesty says NPN; Cabot/diyAudio say PNP). Since the 2024-2026 consolidation, the TI RC4580 die also ships as TI NE5532/LM833/MC33078.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: No comparative listening test or measurement of NJM4580 versus RC4580 was found. The reputation (Soomal, Japanese community) was earned by the JRC part.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - drop-in pinout and similar supply range, with slightly lower GBW on the TI part.

counterfeit_notes: Soomal warns that JRC4580 is often confused with the far cheaper, pin-compatible JRC4558. Relabelling 4558s as 4580s is therefore the plausible main risk, but no documented teardown or measurement case was found, and the discovery claim that 'JRC4580' clones/remarks are common was not confirmed (low confidence). Buy from authorised channels (Mouser, RS, Marutsu, Akizuki, Keisei, Digi-Key). Check that the logo (JRC/NJR/Nisshinbo), laser-marking font and date codes are consistent. Distrust cheap 'NOS' DIP lots, since the DIP NJM4580D is NRND and supply will tighten. D-rank parts appear as 'NJM4580DD' in distributor listings and 'NJM4580D-D' in the 2025 datasheet. Quick bench check: GBW about 15 MHz and slew about 5 V/µs; 4558-class parts are much slower. TI RC4580 is a legitimate but different die (12 MHz GBW).

LM4562 / LME49720: lower distortion, higher-supply modern bipolar
OPA1612 / OPA1602: modern low-noise bipolar duals

revision_chain_notes:
TI SLOS412 (RC4580), oldest to newest: original April 2003 (no copy found) -> A (not found) -> B (not found) -> C (Revised March 2004; Octopart 153412 copies, E2E copy, and a new Octopart 'RC4580' copy titled Rev. C) -> D (Revised November 2014; Mouser, mikroe, Octopart and others) -> E (Revised November 2024; ti.com, plus the new ti.com/lit/pdf/slos412 redirect). A search for 'SLOS412A' OR 'SLOS412B' returned only the C/D/E copies, so no copy of the original, Rev A or Rev B was found. They may never have been published between April 2003 and March 2004, or they may survive only in Wayback captures of focus.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/rc4580.pdf from 2003-2004 (that seed URL follows the TI URL pattern and was not seen in search results). Still missing: the original, A and B.

TI SLOS707 (RC4580-Q1): original December 2010 (no copy found) -> A (Revised July 2012; confirmed by the new Octopart RC4580QPWRQ1 copy 11812388, and a taoic/aliyuncs copy titled Rev. A). No revision later than A was found; ti.com symlink still serves Rev A. Still missing: the December 2010 original.

JRC/NJR/Nisshinbo NJM4580 (Japanese and English): Ver.2003-03-13 (JP; Marutsu, op316, e-ele, confirmed again this round) -> Ver.2012-02-24 (JP; RS) -> Ver.2012-09-14 (EN on Mouser, JP on Akizuki) -> 20250303 (Nisshinbo EN/JP). Searches for Ver. editions before 2003, for 2014/2016/2018 editions, and for editions between 2012 and 2025 (NJR-to-Nisshinbo transition, 2019-2024) found nothing. New copies with the edition not shown: the alldatasheet NJRC series 7453/7454/7455/7457 (5 pages, 248 KB, likely the same early edition as 7451); alldatasheet 1475568 NJM4580CG (7 pages, 372 KB, probably a later and longer edition; worth checking whether it is a 2012-2022 NJR edition); digchip 237 and download id 1078154; datasheetcatalog NJM4580L; the DigiKey htmldatasheet; and RS product pages. Still missing: any pre-2003 JRC edition (the 1990s JRC data book), an English edition before 2012-09-14, and any NJR/Nisshinbo edition between 2012-09-14 and 2025-03-03. Next steps: check the edition inside the alldatasheet 1475568 and digchip 237 copies, and query Wayback for the njr.com / semicon.njr.co.jp seeds.
